source.title_on_document: Training novices to think, or giving them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT

supplement.holds: Design details, rubrics, rater training and inter-rater reliability (Table A.3), idea-extraction and diversity pipeline, descriptive statistics (Table A.7), balance table with arm Ns (Table A.8), and all coefficient tables with clustered SEs (Tables A.9-A.14). No separate online supplement, data, or code is referenced.

paper_design_summary: A preregistered 2x2 factorial RCT with 1,053 first-year undergraduates in 13 classes of an introductory management course at a European university; intact classes were randomized (within program) to a causal-reasoning training game or a placebo game, crossed with ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access or no access, during regular class time. All participants then wrote a recommendation of about 180 words on how to raise alumni awareness and usage of the university's merchandise. Outputs were scored by trained master's-student raters on an awareness-and-usage rubric, by embedding similarity to three expert solutions, by GPT-5 on causal-reasoning attributes, and by an LLM idea-extraction pipeline for number of ideas, within-solution diversity, and between-solution diversity.

studies.label: 2x2 classroom RCT: causal-reasoning training x ChatGPT Edu access (alumni merchandising business case)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Causal-reasoning training game vs placebo game, crossed with ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access vs no access during the business case
assignment.quote: The treatments of our research design are randomized at the class level: we assign one intact class per program to each of the four arms.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix Section 1; also PDF p. 2 [printed p. 1], Introduction
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 17 [printed p. 16], Appendix Section 1 ('pre-registered with the AEA RCT Registry [link currently not available to preserve anonymity]'); PDF p. 3 [printed p. 2], footnote 2

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Placebo game (same 12 questions, no instruction or feedback), no ChatGPT access during the case

arms.name: Causal
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game (12 questions with worked examples and feedback), no ChatGPT access; told 'Remember the skills you learned during the game'

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Placebo game, then ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access in a separate browser tab during the case

arms.name: Causal&GPT
arms.description: Causal-reasoning training game, then ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access during the case; oversampled cell (two M-program classes)

participants.exclusions: No exclusions reported; all regressions use 1,053 observations. Within-solution diversity uses 1,051 because 2 responses contained only one core idea (set to missing). Randomization was of 13 intact classes (4 E&M, 4 E&F, 5 M; one class per program per arm, two M classes in Causal&GPT), so per-person counts reflect class attendance. Footnote 1: 90.5% of participants with GPT access declared compliance (88% GPT only, 92% Causal&GPT).
participants.who: First-year undergraduates in economics & management, economics & finance, and management bachelor programs, in 13 sections of the same introductory management course
participants.country: Not stated in the text (university anonymized as 'a leading European University'); the case and GPT-5 prompt name Bocconi University (Milan, Italy)
participants.quote: In a 2x2 randomized control trial, we assign 1,053 first-year undergraduates in economics, management and finance to one of four conditions
participants.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; arm Ns PDF p. 2 [printed p. 1], Introduction, and PDF p. 43 [printed p. 42], Table A.8

ai_tool.how_used: Participants in AI arms could use ChatGPT Edu in a separate browser tab while writing the case recommendation; non-AI arms were not allowed. Conversation logs were requested in the post-survey.

task.description: Consultant-style written recommendation of up to/approximately 180 words on how to increase alumni awareness and usage of the university's branded merchandise, given operational data on sales channels, pricing, and the 144,000+ alumni base.
task.duration: About 45 minutes (main text: 45 minutes on the case; Appendix: each session lasted approximately 45 minutes)

outcomes.name: Awareness and usage evaluation score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Rubric adapted from the AAU marketing framework: each of 3 (of 20) trained master's-student raters scores awareness and usage on 1-5 anchored scales; rater score = mean of the two; recommendation score = mean across 3 raters (3,159 ratings). Raters are master's students the paper calls 'human experts'; coding as expert_raters is a judgment call (could be human_raters). Overall mean 2.635, SD 0.843 (Table A.7). Robustness: PDS-lasso models adding text, idea, and reasoning controls (Table A.13; GPT 0.490, 0.448, 0.362, all p<0.01). ICC by arm in Table A.3 (Control 0.275, Causal 0.322, GPT 0.534, Causal X GPT 0.493).

contrasts.reported: OLS, SEs clustered (mother tongue x HS type x degree class). GPT 0.834*** (0.100), constant 2.236, no controls; GPT 0.862*** (0.079), constant 2.089, with balance controls; N = 1053. Text: 'relative to the estimated score of 2.09 for the control group'.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 45 [printed p. 44], Table A.10; PDF p. 8 [printed p. 7], Section 4.2; PDF p. 9 [printed p. 8], Figure 3

contrasts.reported: Not printed as one coefficient: equals GPT + Causal x GPT. Causal x GPT 0.072 (0.125) no controls; 0.082 (0.084) with balance controls. SE of the sum not printed.

outcomes.name: Number of ideas in the solution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of distinct core ideas from a consensus LLM extraction (GPT-5.2, 3 prompt variants x 5 runs plus 1 original run; idea confirmed if in at least 2 of 16 runs; uncertain matches adjudicated by GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6). Mean 6.756, SD 3.170 (Table A.7). Figure 5 shows SD-normalized coefficients (GPT 'more than one-half of a standard deviation').

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, clustered SEs (50 clusters): GPT 2.251*** (0.290); constant 4.118; N = 1053. Standardized coefficient shown only in Figure 5.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 1; PDF p. 11 [printed p. 10], Figure 5

contrasts.reported: Not printed as one coefficient: equals GPT + Causal x GPT. Causal x GPT 0.690* (0.357). SE of the sum not printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 1

outcomes.name: Between-solution diversity of ideas
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean cosine distance of a student's core ideas from all other students' ideas in the full sample (higher = more distinct from others). Mean 0.624, SD 0.038 (Table A.7). Figure 5 shows SD-normalized coefficients.

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, clustered SEs (50 clusters): GPT -0.002 (0.002); Causal 0.018*** (0.003); constant 0.597; N = 1053. Text: 'GPT alone and the interaction between Causal and GPT are not distinguishable from zero.'
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 3; PDF p. 11 [printed p. 10], Figure 5 and text

contrasts.reported: Not printed as one coefficient: equals GPT + Causal x GPT. Causal x GPT 0.002 (0.004). Text: 'relative to Causal alone, adding the availability of LLMs does not increase diversity, but it does not kill it either.'
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 3; PDF p. 14 [printed p. 13], Conclusions

diversity_detail.metric: Mean cosine distance between a participant's core-idea embeddings and the core ideas of all other participants (higher = more diverse; no sign reversal needed)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (ideas extracted by GPT-5.2; Italian responses translated to English before embedding)
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant's ideas against all other participants' ideas in the pooled sample of all four arms ('N = 1,052 comparisons per idea'), not against the participant's own arm only
diversity_detail.uncertainty: OLS of the participant-level score on treatment indicators with balance controls; SEs clustered by mother tongue x HS type x degree class (50 clusters), not by the 13 randomized classes
diversity_detail.notes: Because the reference set pools all arms, this is distance from the overall solution space rather than within-arm homogeneity. No within-arm pairwise similarity is reported.

outcomes.name: Within-solution diversity of ideas
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean pairwise cosine distance among the core ideas within one participant's response (text-embedding-3-large); missing for 2 responses with one idea. Mean 0.596, SD 0.078 (Table A.7). Coded flexibility because it is variety among one person's own ideas. Figure 5 shows SD-normalized coefficients.

contrasts.reported: OLS with balance controls, clustered SEs (50 clusters): GPT 0.009** (0.005); Causal 0.043*** (0.006); constant 0.541; N = 1051. Text: 'GPT also has a positive but much smaller effect.'
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 2; PDF p. 11 [printed p. 10], Figure 5 and text

contrasts.reported: Not printed as one coefficient: equals GPT + Causal x GPT. Causal x GPT -0.001 (0.008); text says the interaction 'is instead close to zero'. SE of the sum not printed; direction is the screener's reading.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 46 [printed p. 45], Table A.12 col. 2; PDF p. 11 [printed p. 10]

outcomes.name: Similarity of participant solution to expert solutions (Mkt Professor, Merchandising expert, Expert Alumnus)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1 minus cosine distance (text-embedding-3-large) between each participant's response and each of three expert-written solutions (marketing professor, merchandising manager, alumnus), in the participant's survey language. Three variants of one outcome. Means 0.794 / 0.753 / 0.806, SDs 0.041 / 0.045 / 0.050 (Table A.7). PDS-lasso robustness in Table A.14 (GPT 0.008-0.030, all significant). Measures closeness to expert answers, not creativity or diversity.

contrasts.reported: OLS, clustered SEs, N = 1053. GPT, no controls / with balance controls: Mkt Professor 0.028*** (0.007) / 0.026*** (0.004); Merchandising expert 0.030*** (0.007) / 0.028*** (0.005); Expert Alumnus 0.044*** (0.006) / 0.044*** (0.005).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 45 [printed p. 44], Table A.11; PDF p. 10 [printed p. 9], Figure 4

contrasts.reported: Not printed as one coefficient: equals GPT + Causal X GPT. Causal X GPT (no controls / with controls): 0.003 (0.010) / 0.003 (0.004); -0.007 (0.009) / -0.007 (0.006); -0.002 (0.007) / -0.002 (0.006).

company_involvement.description: Two authors are affiliated with OpenAI (Asirvatham; Chatterji, OpenAI & Duke); Rachel Brown contributed during her employment at OpenAI; Steve Ramos contributed as a paid contractor for OpenAI. The AI tool is OpenAI's ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o), and the scoring pipeline uses OpenAI models (GPT-5, GPT-5.2, text-embedding-3-large). The PDF on file is hosted on cdn.openai.com.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1, author block and footnotes

eligibility.reason: Intact classes (13) were randomized to ChatGPT Edu access vs none (crossed with causal training) for an open-ended business recommendation task with many acceptable answers (idea generation). 1,053 students analyzed (GPT 197 vs Control 249 for the main AI contrast). Outcomes are scored on the written output: rater-scored awareness-and-usage quality (usefulness), number of ideas (fluency), and embedding-based between-participant idea diversity (across_people). Caveats: cluster randomization with only 13 classes (one class per program per arm); SEs are clustered on 50 mother-tongue x HS-type x degree-class cells rather than on the randomized class; the rubric scores marketing effectiveness rather than creativity per se; design class lab_rct vs field_rct is a judgment call (in-class, proctored, ungraded session).

one_line_finding: ChatGPT access raised rater scores of the recommendations (GPT 0.862, SE 0.079, vs control constant 2.089 on a 1-5 scale) and the number of ideas (2.251, SE 0.290) but did not change between-participant idea diversity (-0.002, SE 0.002), while causal training raised it (0.018, SE 0.003) (Tables A.10 and A.12, PDF pp. 45-46).
open_questions: Design class: the experiment ran during regular class hours under proctor supervision, unannounced and apparently ungraded; field_rct (coursework setting) vs lab_rct (supervised session) needs a ruling.

Standard errors are clustered on 50 mother tongue x high-school type x degree-class cells, not on the 13 randomized classes; whether these SEs qualify under codebook section 10 for clustered assignment is unclear.

Between-solution diversity is each participant's distance from all other participants pooled across arms, not within-arm homogeneity; it may not match the codebook's 'main semantic-similarity measure across all participants in each arm' for the across_people primary record.
Which AI contrast is primary: GPT vs Control (both placebo game) is the plain ai_vs_bau; Causal&GPT vs Causal is not printed as a single coefficient (sum of GPT and interaction without its SE).
Whether the awareness-and-usage rubric (marketing effectiveness) counts as a creativity/usefulness outcome for pooling, and whether master's-student raters are expert_raters or human_raters.
Arm-level means and SDs are not reported; only regression coefficients, overall SDs (Table A.7), and SD-normalized coefficients in figures.
notes: PDF page = printed page + 1. Arm counts (249/256/197/351) appear in the Introduction and Table A.8; the abstract says 1,053 were assigned. GPT compliance self-declared at 90.5% (footnote 1, PDF p. 2). AI (ChatGPT Edu) was available to the treatment arms while they wrote the scored recommendation. PDS-lasso decompositions (Tables A.13-A.14) are robustness/mediation analyses and are summarized in measure_detail rather than listed as separate outcomes.
